newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged on Tuesday, based on market orders at 1018 EST, traders said.
Today's spec/hedge report showed the speculators to be holding a 51.9 percent net short position in the market, confirming that a short-covering rally is likely, analysts said.
Nearby resistance was pegged at 74.00 cents basis July, followed by 75.00 cents.

Prices ended little changed on Monday, with the most-active July contract closing 0.04 cent higher at 73.53 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.70 to 73.20 cents. New-crop December finished up 0.19 at 75.96 cents.
Support was pegged at 73.00 cents in July.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture said Monday that 21 percent of the U.S. crop has been planted, compared with 19 percent last year and 24 percent according to the five-year average.
Still, players remain concerned about planting delays throughout the cotton belt, particularly in Texas where cold wet conditions have prompted several farmers to switch to other crops.
